fatal_errors: The proposed AlNbTiZr medium-entropy coating is materially different from the target AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy coating, eliminating the Cr-dependent protective oxide mechanism.
The cited evidence concerns corrosion protection under PWR operating conditions and does not establish performance during an approximately 800 °C high-temperature steam exposure.
The proposed Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 scale is inconsistent with the target protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite scale.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies compositional optimization near 10 at.% Al as a potentially nonmonotonic way to reduce oxidation and oxygen penetration, and it proposes a reasonably discriminating composition-series experiment with an explicit falsification rule. However, it reconstructs a different coating system and oxide chemistry. It also tests at 800 °C rather than the demonstrated 1000 °C/60 min and 1100 °C/30 min steam conditions, omits coating thickness and steam-flow constraints, and does not capture the target mechanism involving Ti/Cr enrichment, preferential Al2O3/TiO2 formation, Cr2O3 stabilization, or detrimental Al-Ti/Al-Zr intermetallic formation at high Al. Most importantly, E1 supports the selected AlNbTiZr composition and oxide phases under service-corrosion conditions, but not the claimed accident-temperature steam resistance, so the central high-temperature claim is an unsupported extrapolation.
